clue.text: Pelt Chicago footballers with blood

parts.note: the Chicago Bears are an American football team
blood means family, kin

explanation.surface: Someone pelts a Chicago football team with blood, as if in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb meaning throw at, but it is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is the fur hide of a bear, a pelt in the noun sense.

clue.text: Tense BBC head entered in the out-of-date returns

indicators.note: one piece going into another, so the boss's letters sit within the old word
returns signals the archaic article is read backwards

parts.note: ye is the old-fashioned form of the
the head of the BBC is its Director General, DG

explanation.surface: A nervous BBC chief steps into a programme of old repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's boss is its Director General, DG; 'returns' reverses the archaic 'ye' (as in Ye Olde Shoppe) to EY, and 'entered in' puts DG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy and tense are synonyms for nervous and on edge.

clue.text: It's a commonplace to replace one with ring plant protector

indicators.note: replace says one letter is swapped out for another in the word for a commonplace
with names the incoming letter in this substitution

parts.note: a commonplace is a trite saying, a cliche
one is the Roman numeral I
a ring is round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gardener's tip: change a hackneyed saying for a ring-shaped plant cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of CLICHE for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a bell-shaped glass or plastic cover put over young plants to shield them from frost.

clue.text: Small defensive building taking pressure off fight

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
feeling off means ill
to fight with fists is to box

explanation.surface: A little fort that takes the strain out of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the three pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillbox is a small concrete guard post, often with gun slits, used in wartime fortifications.

clue.text: Ellis's fancy alcove in Hong Kong?

definitions.note: the definition is the first name belonging to Ellis, the writer Havelock Ellis

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Ellis owned an ornate nook somewhere in Hong Kong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'Ellis's': Havelock Ellis was a British writer on human sexuality. 'fancy' rearranges the nook to AVELOC, and 'in' sets it within the territory's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Havelock was the given name of the psychologist Havelock Ellis, so it is what is Ellis's.

clue.text: Ban on the very people who frequent this dating venue?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed beneath, so the word for ban sits under the customers

parts.words: the very people who frequent this
parts.note: the customers of such a venue are unattached people, singles
a bar is a ban or prohibition

explanation.surface: A dating spot oddly bans the very customers it exists for.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the place exists for the people it seems to bar; 'on' in a down clue puts BAR beneath SINGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A singles bar is a pub or club where unattached people go to meet potential partners.

clue.text: Outburst unfortunately seen by disheartened Zeke?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled
disheartened means the heart is removed, leaving only the outside letters of the name

explanation.surface: Zeke, feeling low, was caught having an emotional outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges SEEN to SNEE; 'disheartened' strips Zeke to ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden involuntary burst of air through the nose, an outburst in a literal sense.

clue.text: Capital Henry put into Virgin store

parts.note: virgin as an adjective means new, untouched

indicators.note: put into places the unit symbol inside the shop word

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food store
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry gets a job at a Virgin store in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Virgin the retail brand, but it is simply NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the seat of government and capital city of India.

clue.text: Having no leader, abuse ally

indicators.note: no leader means the first letter of the word for abuse is dropped

parts.note: to abuse someone verbally is to malign them

explanation.surface: With no one in charge, people turn on their own ally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no leader' drops the M from MALIGN; 'ally' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To align yourself with someone is to ally with them, joining their side.

clue.text: Speak harshly of 'underwear yen'

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone talks scornfully about a craving for lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'yen' that looks like a longing is the currency, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To bray is to talk loudly and harshly, like a donkey's cry.

clue.text: Associates pass old measures

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
leagues are old units of distance, about three miles each

explanation.surface: Business partners hand over old-fashioned measuring tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' is not a verb here but a noun, a mountain col.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleagues are fellow workers, people one is associated with professionally.

clue.text: Capital generated from second football stand at outskirts of Jacksonville

parts.note: the Kop is a famous terraced stand at Liverpool's Anfield ground, and the name for such stands generally

indicators.note: outskirts means only the outermost letters of the city name are used

explanation.surface: A capital's wealth said to come from a football stand and a US city's suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A Kop is a steep stand of terracing at a British football ground, named after Spion Kop in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the capital city of North Macedonia.

clue.text: 24 stirred in Inca prepared for a different civilisation

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the answer to 24 Down, a woman's name meaning optimism
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman mixing into Inca culture is ready for another ancient civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HOPE (24 Down), IN and INCA are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenicians were an ancient seafaring Mediterranean people, a civilisation other than the Incas.

clue.text: Instrument revealing Frodo met Erik, essentially

indicators.note: revealing means showing what is concealed within the following words
essentially points to the core letters of the phrase, inside its outer letters

explanation.surface: A device that shows the moment Frodo met someone called Erik.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across frODO MET ERik.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is the gauge in a vehicle that records the distance travelled.

clue.text: Buries notes about retaining storage capacity

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
about means around in a muddled way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB is a megabyte, a measure of computer storage capacity

explanation.surface: Someone hides away memos about how much a hard drive can store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like the musical letters but is anagram fodder: 'about' gives ENTOS, and 'retaining' holds the megabyte inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombs means puts in a tomb, so it is a synonym for buries.

clue.text: Familiar form of address associated with virile male, inwardly independent, living an unconventional life

parts.note: bo is an informal American term of address, like buddy

indicators.note: inwardly means placed within, so the letter for independent goes inside

parts.note: a he-man is a strong, macho man

explanation.surface: A long description of a friendly macho free spirit who goes his own way.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo is chiefly American, like buddy. 'inwardly' sets the I within the he-man, making HEMIAN, and 'associated with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian is an artistic free spirit who rejects conventional social norms and lifestyle.

clue.text: Robert, engaged in sloppy kiss, goes downhill

indicators.note: engaged in means locked inside, so one piece sits within another
sloppy means careless and messy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Bob is a short form of the name Robert

explanation.surface: Robert, caught in a wet kiss, sees things go downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes downhill' sounds like decline, but it is literal: riding on snow. 'sloppy' makes SKIS, and 'engaged in' places Robert's short name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A skibob is a bike-like vehicle with skis for wheels, ridden down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Research place over upright castle

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a place for research
upright means honest and principled, moral

explanation.surface: A science facility sits above a tall castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LAB to BAL; 'upright' is moral, not vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the British royal family's castle in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Pioneering South African TV series fan?

definitions.meaning: a pioneer who took part in the Great Trek of Boer settlers in nineteenth-century South Africa
a fan of the science-fiction TV series Star Trek

explanation.surface: A trailblazing South African turns out to love a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers who made the Great Trek were trekkers, and fans of Star Trek call themselves Trekkers.

clue.text: Digger's board

definitions.meaning: a digger in the sense of something that digs ditches or trenches, with 's for is
a wooden board or platter once used to serve food

explanation.surface: A miner owns a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch-cutting machine is a trencher, and so was a medieval wooden serving plate.

clue.text: Capri altogether too much as a tourist attraction

indicators.note: too much says the phrase has more letters than needed, so the answer is buried within it

explanation.surface: Capri is simply overdone as a holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across capRI ALTOgether.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto Bridge over Venice's Grand Canal is one of the city's most visited sights.

clue.text: It's a pleasure to cultivate, taking little time

indicators.note: taking means absorbing, so the short unit goes inside the farming word

parts.note: to till is to cultivate land
HR is a short form of hour, a small amount of time

explanation.surface: Gardening, even in brief spells, is a real delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little time' is HR, the abbreviation for hour, put inside TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement and delight, a pleasure.

clue.text: Tower's shaky, utter rubbish top

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order
top in a down clue means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wobbly tower is absolute junk at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes R from rubbish, and 'shaky' rearranges it with UTTER. The 's on Tower is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A turret is a small tower on a castle or larger building.

clue.text: Light manufacturer's union organiser

parts.note: a match is something used to make a light
a manufacturer is a maker, with 's for is

explanation.surface: A firm that makes lighting runs the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union; it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker arranges marriages or romantic partnerships, the unions of couples.

clue.text: Criminal hiding ring in trough

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the circle letter goes inside

parts.note: a hod is a trough on a pole for carrying bricks
a ring is round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A villain stashes a ring in a water trough.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is the open box a bricklayer's labourer carries on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is slang, short for hoodlum, for a gangster or criminal.

clue.text: Name of woman parking in garden

indicators.note: in places the parking letter inside the gardening word

parts.note: to garden is to hoe, working soil
P is the symbol for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Identifying a woman who parks in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here: to hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a female first name, from the virtue of optimism.

clue.text: It's so long, to accommodate one's top jewellery

indicators.note: accommodate means find room for, so one piece goes inside the farewell

parts.note: ta-ra is an informal British goodbye, like so long
one is I, with 's for has

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye while finding space for someone's best jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ra is northern English slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled band worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Ideal version of Mexican pearl one's able to 'disappear'

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking of it, so these letters are rearranged
disappear says some letters vanish from the anagram pool

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to be able is to be capable, can

explanation.surface: A perfect Mexican pearl that can vanish like a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and CAN from MEXICAN PEARL and rearrange MEXPEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect model or example to follow, an ideal.
